quote: 5.27 ± 0.45 was our own K from v7–v11 pasted into the wrong column, and the "same semi-amplitude" argument was the centre of the comparison.
description: The comparison said HD 105779 b has the same semi-amplitude as HD 297396 b (5.27 ± 0.45 m/s), but that number was this paper's own K pasted into the wrong column; the source gives 10.42 ± 0.96 m/s, so the central 'same semi-amplitude' argument was wrong.

The HD 103891 b values in the comparison (K = 14.78 ± 0.30 m/s, K/σK 49, ΔlnZ +86.5) did not match the source paper's adopted results (the evidence was their DRS value); the correct values are K = 21.12 ± 0.86, K/σK 24.6, ΔlnZ +94.3.

quote: Baluev = 4.9e-5, "30× more optimistic than the bootstrap, so we do not use it"
description: The Baluev analytic false-alarm probability was computed wrongly (4.9e-5, said to be 30 times below the bootstrap, which an upper bound cannot be) and the 103-epoch FAP was an extrapolated ≈3e-6; correct values are 2.2e-3 and 6.7e-6, in agreement with the bootstrap.

quote: 34.1 d is 8 × P0, pasted from the harmonic list.
description: The convective turnover time was given as 34.1 d (with Rossby numbers 0.84, and 0.13 at P0), a number pasted from the harmonic list; the project's own kinematics file gives 23.7 d (Rossby 1.21, and 0.18 at P0).

quote: "R_p ≈ 2.5 R⊕ at this mass [Chen & Kipping]", 960 ppm
description: The planet radius from the Chen & Kipping mass-radius relation was given as 2.5 R⊕ (960 ppm transit depth), but the relation gives 3.4 R⊕ (1800 ppm) at 11.8 Earth masses.

quote: C2 rejects 1 spectrum
description: The data-selection section said criterion C2 rejects one spectrum, but the script flags two (one of which also fails C4), so two are rejected.

quote: The ±1.0 left out the orbital-phase uncertainty
description: The out-of-sample prediction was given as 5.5 ± 1.0 m/s (a '≈1.2σ test'), but the uncertainty left out the orbital-phase term; corrected to 5.2 ± 2.7 m/s, about a 1σ test.

quote: "period held constant to about ±1 min"
description: The phase-stability result was stated ambiguously as a period held constant to about ±1 min; it now says 3 parts in 10^5, about one minute for a 30-d rotation period.

quote: "semi-amplitude is four times the per-epoch error"
description: The text said the semi-amplitude is four times the per-epoch error, which is true only of the median formal error; with jitter the per-epoch scatter (4–6 m/s) is comparable to K.

quote: "gap at 1.8–3 au where no probe is sensitive"
description: The companion-exclusion section claimed a gap at 1.8–3 au where no probe is sensitive, but the radial velocities themselves exclude stellar and brown-dwarf companions there.

quote: Gaia reflex 0.34 μas
description: The expected Gaia astrometric reflex motion was miscalculated as 0.34 μas instead of 0.05 μas (conclusion unchanged).

quote: Bonferroni 0.0057
description: The Bonferroni threshold was given as 0.0057 instead of 0.05/9 = 0.0056.

quote: 2.59 is the once-exceeded level, not the expected maximum.
description: The expected largest |z| among 103 draws was given as 2.59, which is the level exceeded once on average, not the expected maximum (2.7).

quote: "Δχ² = 44.6 before the NZP correction"
description: A single Δχ² of 44.6 was quoted for the fit before the nightly zero-point correction, but that is the 103-epoch value; the two data sets give 31.9 and 44.6.

quote: 3.7 nats = "1.5 times the run-to-run scatter"
description: The 3.7-nat evidence difference was called 1.5 times the run-to-run scatter, but it is about twice the 1.7-nat scatter.

quote: 200.9-d evidence "+3.85 after the prior-width correction"
description: The 200.9-d signal's evidence was described as '+3.85 after the prior-width correction', implying the same prior as planet b, but its period prior was widened to 10–1000 d, not 1.05–1000 d, and that prior was missing from Table A.1.
Table 7 gave 91 radial velocities for HD 103891, but the source paper uses 90 (the authors removed one).
Table 7 gave the minimum mass of HD 103891 b with an uncertainty of ±0.02 instead of the source paper's +0.06/−0.05.

quote: P/P_rot > 48
description: Table 7 gave the orbital-to-rotation period ratio limit for HD 103891 b as > 48 instead of > 47.

quote: HD 105779 e < 0.16 unlabelled
description: Table 7 gave eccentricity limits without their confidence levels, so HD 105779 b's 1σ limit (< 0.16) sat beside HD 22496 b's 95 % limit (< 0.15) as if they were comparable.

quote: HD 22496 "9 % semi-amplitude from 41 epochs"
description: HD 22496 b's semi-amplitude precision, baseline and coherence were described as coming from 41 ESPRESSO epochs over 895 d ('9 %', '895 d', 'no 895-d data set could bound' the coherence), but the source's K comes from a joint ESPRESSO+HARPS fit spanning 17 yr (8 % from ESPRESSO plus 43 HARPS points); this includes the Table 7 baseline entry listed under E16.

quote: companions excluded "0.02–100 au"
description: The abstract and Sect. 5.8 claimed companions are excluded from 0.02 to 100 au, but the speckle contrast curves typically stop near 1.2″ (about 55 au).

quote: A draft argument comparing a 350-d "evolution time" with the P0 coherence was dropped after the referee check
description: A v13 draft argued from a comparison of a 350-d Gaussian-process 'evolution time' with the coherence at P0, but the timescale of a nearly aperiodic kernel is not a spot lifetime, so the argument was dropped.

quote: the −2.93-nat "eccentric disfavoured" result with all epochs is flagged as unreliable
description: The circular orbit was justified by an all-epoch evidence result ('eccentric disfavoured', −2.93 nats) that turned out to be unreliable; the circular orbit is now justified by the 103-epoch limit.

quote: P_rot is "estimated", not "bounded"
description: The rotation period was described as 'bounded', although it only comes from activity calibrations; it is now 'estimated'.

quote: "none of 612 other HARPS stars" (not "no other HARPS star")
description: The abstract claimed that no other HARPS star shows the signal, which is broader than the 612 stars actually checked.

quote: the aperture ASAS-SN photometry does show 11.9 mmag at P0
description: The abstract implied the ASAS-SN photometry shows no variability at P0, but the aperture photometry does show 11.9 mmag there; the claim holds only for the saturation-corrected photometry.

quote: "the amplitude the data would detect nine times in ten" (not "the largest permitted")
description: The abstract said the forward model used the largest permitted amplitude, but it used the amplitude the data would detect nine times in ten.

quote: v12 said "same amplitude"; 6.5 ± 0.7 vs 4.9 ± 0.9
description: The held-out programme-split test claimed the two groups give the same amplitude, but they agree only within 1.4σ (6.5 ± 0.7 vs 4.9 ± 0.9 m/s).

quote: v12 said "every treatment gives a detection"
description: Sect. 6 claimed every analysis treatment gives a detection, but under the full-band prior the weakest cells are indecisive.

quote: "stronger than any spot model in its coherence, not in its harmonic content"
description: The forward-model conclusion was stated too broadly; the signal is stronger than any spot model only in its coherence, not in its harmonic content.

quote: spot patterns evolve over one to a few rotations (v12: "about one")
description: The coherence argument said spot patterns evolve over about one rotation, but the supportable statement is one to a few rotations.

quote: 200.9-d signal: added that its strength is a caution in its own right.
description: The discussion of the 200.9-d second signal lacked the caveat that its strength is itself a reason for caution.

quote: Cross-star control: states it is not matched in spectral type or mask.
description: The cross-star control was presented without saying that the comparison stars are not matched in spectral type or mask.

quote: "Metal-rich" → "near-solar metallicity" ([Fe/H] = +0.11 ± 0.12)
description: The star was called metal-rich although its [Fe/H] = +0.11 ± 0.12 is near-solar.

quote: v12: "mass below 5 %"
description: The ESPRESSO follow-up plan promised a mass below 5 %, which the 6 % stellar-mass uncertainty makes impossible.

quote: Abstract and Summary give the full FAP/FIP range
description: The v13 abstract and Summary did not give the full range of false-alarm and false-inclusion probabilities across data sets and noise models, only part of it.

quote: Pre-registration language cut to one sentence stating the deposit postdates the runs
description: v13 used pre-registration language ('written down before') in several sections and Table 1, although the deposit postdates the analysis runs.

quote: Title has no "strong", says "Neptune-mass"
description: The v13 title described the detection as 'strong', more than the evidence supports.

quote: v13's "a few per cent" was also wrong and is gone.
description: v13 promised that one ESPRESSO season would give the semi-amplitude to a few per cent, but with the fitted 3–4 m/s stellar jitter 40 epochs give only a 6–8σ detection.

quote: v13 called U(18, 25) and U(5, 15) period priors
description: The v13 footnote on Sreenivas et al.'s priors called U(18, 25) and U(5, 15) period priors, but they are that paper's semi-amplitude (K) priors.

quote: v13's CHANGELOG said P and T_conj were anti-correlated
description: v13 treated its 0.09-orbit phase-uncertainty bound as conservative on the assumption that P and T_conj are anti-correlated, but the posterior shows a positive correlation (+0.34) and direct propagation gives 0.088–0.092, so the text now says within 0.1 of an orbit.

quote: every analysis choice came after the signal was found (Sect. 2.2)
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat that every analysis choice was made after the signal was found.

quote: the full-band cells that are indecisive (Sect. 6)
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the statement that some full-band-prior cells of Sect. 6 are indecisive.

quote: "at amplitudes the data allow" for the 70 000 simulations
description: The v14 abstract and Summary dropped the qualifier that the 70 000 simulations were run at amplitudes the data allow.

quote: the correlated-noise qualifier on "least favourable"
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the correlated-noise qualifier on a 'least favourable' statement.

quote: the cross-star sample is not matched in spectral type or mask
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat that the cross-star control sample is not matched in spectral type or mask.

quote: Nava et al. (2020) on non-harmonic activity peaks
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat, citing Nava et al. (2020), that stellar activity can produce peaks that are not rotation harmonics.

quote: K is comparable to the per-epoch scatter
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat that the semi-amplitude is comparable to the per-epoch scatter.

quote: the screens describe past failures, not every failure
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat that the failure screens describe past failures, not every possible failure.

quote: the block-activity test is weak
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat that the block-activity test is weak.

quote: HD 47186 b and HD 181433 b were loud signals around quieter stars
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat that the comparison planets HD 47186 b and HD 181433 b were loud signals around quieter stars.

quote: 36–42 d is a candidate rotation period, not a measurement
description: The v14 rewrite dropped the caveat that 36–42 d is a candidate rotation period, not a measurement.

quote: "phases agree to within 1°" (now the two measured phases)
description: The v14 draft said the two programme groups' phases agree to within 1°; it now gives the two measured phases.

quote: "the window cannot make P0" (now what separates the two signals)
description: The v14 draft said the observing window cannot produce P0; it now states what separates the two signals instead.

quote: Table 5 "Noise fluctuation" verdict is now "disfavoured"
description: Table 5's verdict for the 'noise fluctuation' alternative was misstated in the v14 draft and is now 'disfavoured'.

quote: the order of the >100 / >47 ratios
description: The v14 draft gave the >100 and >47 period-ratio limits in the wrong order.

quote: the corner caption
description: The caption of the new corner plot of the adopted-model posterior contained an error that was fixed.

quote: the FIP-frame agreement (1 nat same code, about 2 nats juliet)
description: The v14 draft misstated how closely the FIP results in different frames agree; corrected to 1 nat with the same code and about 2 nats with juliet.

quote: "written rule" wording
description: The v14 draft's wording about a 'written rule' (a decision rule fixed in advance) was corrected.

quote: the CDS footnote ("in full")
description: The wording of the new CDS footnote was wrong and was corrected to say the table is available 'in full'.

quote: v14 fed the PHOENIX-based RVBank value (−4.64) into the Noyes relation and got 28.6 d.
description: v14 estimated the rotation period (28.6 d, candidate range 25–40 d) by feeding the PHOENIX-scale RVBank activity index (−4.64) into a relation calibrated on the Mount Wilson scale; on the right scale it is about 39 d (31–49 d), so the rotation-dependent tests were rerun over 30–50 d.

quote: The radius 0.93 $R_\oplus$ (l. 208) and predicted $K$ 0.4 m s⁻¹ (l. 882) contradict the new 193 ppm depth.
description: The TOI-6263.01 radius (0.93 R⊕), the 130-ppm depth computed from it and the predicted K (0.4 m/s, with the Hill-radius spacing) came from the TOI catalogue radius, which assumes a smaller star; with this paper's stellar radius and the ExoFOP depth the radius is 1.12 R⊕ and K about 0.8 m/s (merges N1, N2, S1 and CHANGELOG_v15 'Found, not on the list' item 2).

quote: Numbers derived from the old range were not updated
description: After the adopted rotation range changed from 25–40 d to 30–50 d, eight statements in the first v15 build stayed on the superseded range: the '55 rotations' count, the Table 5 spot signature, the HD 181433 b 'regime', 'no harmonic at P0', 'every test repeated over 17–45 d', the unstated ASAS-SN 40–50 d gap, the two-month photometric plan simulated at 28 d, and the Fig. 6 run and caption (merges N3 and S2–S9, referee 5.4, CHANGELOG_v15 trade-offs 4–5 and 'Found' item 4).

quote: The ninth-harmonic "worst case" cannot reproduce the signal by construction, so it does not test the scenario it is presented as testing
description: The first v15 build said simulations with the rotation period at nine times P0 do not reproduce the signal (Sect. 5.3, Tables 5 and 7, Summary, and attached to the 150 000-simulation headline), but the quasi-periodic kernel puts under 1 % of its variance in the ninth harmonic, so that simulation could not have reproduced it (merges S10, referee 4b and 5.1, CHANGELOG_v15 trade-off 3).

quote: The column holds the RVBank (PHOENIX-based) values (median −4.644), not the −4.79 now quoted as the activity level.
description: The ancillary data ReadMe did not say that its logRHK column is on the PHOENIX-based RVBank scale rather than the Mount Wilson scale of the −4.79 now quoted in the paper.

quote: The comment says bands 22–40/11–20/7.33–13.33 and $U(22,40)$, but the code uses 30–50.
description: The header comment of the released script rot3050.py described the 22–40 d run although the code uses 30–50 d.

quote: The other columns (−4.94, −5.20, −5.01) must be on the same scale.
description: The comparison table (Table 6) mixed activity scales, with HD 297396 on the Mount Wilson scale and the comparison stars' log R'HK from other sources; all are now Gomes da Silva et al. (2021) medians (merges S13 and CHANGELOG_v15 'Found' item 3).

quote: "its mean activity is −4.79"
description: Sect. 3.2 called −4.79 the star's mean activity level, but it is the median (the weighted mean is −4.81).

quote: "1.2″ or 55 au": the outer edge of the table is 1.175″ = 54.2 au.
description: The outer edge of the measured Zorro contrast curve was given as 1.2″ or 55 au, but the table ends at 1.175″, 54 au.

quote: "the 20 % expected before the pipeline errors were known" has no provenance.
description: The held-out test's prior power was quoted as exactly 20 % with no recorded calculation; recomputation gives 17–21 %, so it now reads 'about 20 %' with provenance.

quote: "Agree with the ephemeris" overstates the result
description: The abstract and Summary said the three post-archive HARPS spectra agree with the ephemeris, but the contrast is carried by one low-S/N spectrum and the test had little power, so it now says they are consistent with the ephemeris but cannot test it.

quote: C3 is not "passed", it cannot be applied
description: The held-out section said the new spectra pass selection criterion C3, but C3 cannot be applied to spectra taken without a simultaneous reference.

quote: The freeze is attested only by the author's records
description: The held-out section said the decision rule was fixed in the released code before the velocities were read, without saying that this date is attested only by the author's records and not independently time-stamped.

quote: `heldout_v15.py` treats the 0.98 m s⁻¹ nightly zero point as fully correlated across the three nights.
description: The secondary held-out comparison script treated the nightly zero-point scatter as shared by all three nights instead of independent per night (the result does not change).

quote: The ±0.1 dex range is therefore a lower limit on the uncertainty.
description: The new rotation estimate understated its uncertainty: the star lies near the red edge of both activity-rotation calibrations, and the weighted-mean activity gives 40 d (32–51 d), beyond the adopted 30–50 d.

quote: l. 286–289 attributes "makes cool stars appear more active" to Perdelwitz et al. (2024).
description: Sect. 3.2 attributed the statement that the PHOENIX-based correction makes cool stars appear more active to Perdelwitz et al. (2024), which the referee could not confirm from that paper.

quote: Table 2 footnote *a* is attached to the B−V row but describes the $S$-index conversion.
description: A Table 2 footnote describing the S-index conversion was attached to the B−V row.

quote: Sect. 5.3 (l. 652–660) uses "evolution time" and "harmonic complexity $w$" without defining the kernel.
description: Sect. 5.3 used the evolving-spot model parameters 'evolution time' and 'harmonic complexity w' without defining the Gaussian-process kernel they belong to.

quote: Yu et al. (2024) is weak evidence either way
description: The new citation of Yu et al. (2024) lacked the caveat that their data end in 2015 and they recovered periods for only 49 of 268 stars, so it is weak evidence either way.

quote: "Every number in the paper is produced by a released script" is contradicted by NUMBERS.md
description: The generative-AI statement claimed every number in the paper is produced by a released script, but some come from pipeline outputs, published values and hand arithmetic.

quote: "implemented twice, in independent code" should say that both implementations were written with the same AI assistance
description: The generative-AI statement called the two Gaussian-process implementations independent code without saying that both were written with AI assistance.

quote: The DOI is wrong. 10.1051/0004-6361/202348621 resolves to Vohl et al.
description: The Perdelwitz et al. (2024) bibliography entry carried the DOI of a different paper.

quote: The subtitle is wrong.
description: The Astudillo-Defru et al. (2017) bibliography entry had the wrong subtitle.
